title.narrative: Leading from The South (2021-2025)

description.narrative: Leading from the South (LFS) is a ground-breaking partnership between the Dutch Government and a consortium of southern-led feminist Women’s Funds (WFs): the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF), FIMI-AYNI – the International Indigenous Women’s Fund (FIMI), Fondo de Mujeres del Sur (FMS) and the Women’s Fund Asia (WFA). As Leading from the South 1.0 (LFS 1.0) has demonstrated,there are significant gains to be realised from southern-led, feminist WFs funding Southern Women’s Rights Organisations (SWROs) to determine how best to address injustice and unequal power relations in their own communities. In particular, supporting SWROs to advocate and lobby for change, has beenvital to achieving gender equality. The Dutch Ministry for Foreign Affairs has, through the StrengtheningCivil Society Framework and the SDG5 Fund, approved the continuation of LFS.Leveraging the successes and lessons of LFS 1.0, Leading from the South 2.0 (LFS 2.0) will strengthen the LFS Consortium as a feminist funding alliance, led by WFs in the Global South. LFS 2.0 will work across multiple regions, including the West African Sahel, the Horn of Africa, the Middle East and North Africa, the Great Lakes region, Asia, the Pacific and Latin America and the Caribbean, and with a global focus on the leadership and advocacy of indigenous women.Women’s Fund Asia is a regional women’s fund, committed to supporting women, girls, trans, and intersex people led interventions to enhance and strengthen access to their human rights. Established in 2004 as the South Asia Women’s Fund, the fund was created to address the lack of resources for smaller grassroots organisations in South Asia. In March 2018, SAWF transformed into Women’s Fund Asia, with a bigger mandate to fund rights-based work across 18 countries in Asia. Our core mandate is to support women, girls, trans, and intersex rights groups and activists in Asia, address the non-availability of resources for rights work for these constituencies across the region, and support strategies and interventions designed, implemented and led by women, girls, trans, and intersex people.We provide fiscal and technical support to our partners, working to advance women, girls, trans, and intersex rights in their contexts. We aim to move towards developing a regional mandate, which is informed by national and sub-regional realities, and is responsive to the rights and needs of individual women, girls, trans, and intersex people. In the LFS programme, WFA specifically focuses on supporting Asia based SWROs and supporting the activists and organizations in the Pacific in their journey towards the inception of the regional Pacific Feminist Fund.
Please do refer to our data exclusion statement for understanding the rationale in the current design in sharing of the information under LFS reporting in IATI

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its policy framework, clearly articulated the overarching policy principle of Leading from the South as enhancing capabilities of CSOs to fulfil lobbying and advocacy with the following three goals: 1. Prevention and elimination of sexual and gender-based violence against women and girls;2. Strengthening women’s leadership and women’s participation in (political) decision-making;3. Strengthening women’s economic empowerment and improving the economic climate forwomen.

The target group of this program is small, medium, and large southern women´s rights organizations (SWROs) in urban, rural, and regional contexts, working on the human rights of women, girls and trans people to advocate for the full achievement of gender equality and other human rights in the Global South. LFS 2.0 will have a particular focus on women, girls and trans people as change agents, and support women’s rights activism and lobbying efforts in the thematic areas of sexual and gender-based violence, economic security and justice, and leadership and participation.

policy-marker.narrative: Strengthening Civil Society is the overarching policy framework for the grant instruments under policy article 3 of chapter XVII of the central government budget of MFA. The focus of this policy is on civic space, to make it possible for civil society organisations to make their full contribution to achieving the SDGs.The LFS program is specifically under the SDG 5 Fund and also contributes directly to their women's rights and gender equality framework.

comment.narrative: The baseline information for this program was collected as a part of the application form and was completed by all applicants. This data was derived from the final shortlist of 45 applications. It is important to note, that the primary criteria for qualifying for LFS grant is that they are rooted in the feminist and/or other relevant social justice movements and have experience of undertaking lobbying and advocacy work. This aspect of embeddedness and experience is reflected in the above average to high baseline numbers. For us, the aim of LFS this year has been to further contribute to deepening the work being undertaken by the groups in the region. This has meant that the most important task has been to ensure resource support to these groups, so that there is no further roll-back on rights-based organizing, especially in this extremely politically hostile anti-rights context.
